mac.fdag.s3.text: Press “+” and choose SuriClean in Applications, or drag the icon from Finder into the list. If it's already there and ticked, remove it with “–” and add it again: it belonged to the old version.
mac.fdag.s4.text: As soon as macOS grants it, I'll see it by myself ♡ If it asks you to “Quit & Reopen”, that's totally fine.
mac.fdag.yes: Yatta~! Now I have the house keys 🔑✨
mac.fdag.yes.text: Now I can also see Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Trash bins, Mail, Messages and other users' folders. If something stays locked, restart me: macOS sometimes applies it only on reopening.

site.feat.ai_text: Old Claude Code and Codex sessions, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code caches, downloaded models.
site.feat.android_text: WhatsApp and Telegram media, duplicate photos, forgotten APKs, sleeping apps and every app's cache in one tap.
site.feat.apps_text: Apps you haven't opened in ages, with all their hidden data. And those 12 GB macOS installers!
site.feat.big_text: The big monsters of 100 MB and up, sorted from the chubbiest.
site.feat.cache_text: Magic crumbs that grow back by themselves: app and browser caches, logs, temporary files.
site.feat.deps_text: node_modules, venv, target and bin/obj of projects idle for months. They regenerate with one command.
site.feat.dups_text: Duplicates confirmed with SHA-256. Suri always keeps at least one copy 💎.
site.feat.git_text: Checks remote, changes, stashes and unpushed commits. Clean up branches and stashes one by one.
site.feat.map_text: Where did all the GB go? A folder tree with sizes, to spot the big beasts right away.
site.feat.system_text: System logs and crash reports, temporary files, already-installed updates, dumps, Windows.old, old snaps and packages. Just one password.
site.feat.update_text: Checks GitHub and installs new versions without bothering you.
site.features_sub: Fourteen dig zones. Everything that's safe is already preselected, the rest is up to you.
site.footer_first_open: First launch on Mac: right-click the app › Open. On Windows: “More info” › “Run anyway”.
site.footer_made: Made with ♡ by Marco Ricupero and a meerkat
site.marquee: ✦ App caches ✦ Claude & Codex ✦ Forgotten node_modules ✦ Git repos ✦ Twin files ✦ Disk map ✦ System areas ✦ Old installers ✦ Sleeping apps
site.meta_desc: SuriClean: the kawaii meerkat that frees up space on your computer and phone. For Mac, Windows, Ubuntu and Android. Free and open source.
site.ribbon_html: ☆ NEW 新発売 Free for Mac · Windows · Ubuntu · Android ☆
site.safe1_html: Everything goes to the Trash: you can always change your mind.
site.safe2_html: It always asks for confirmation before moving anything.
site.safe3_html: Git repos are touched only if they're safe on the remote; the command to clone them again is saved.
site.safe4_html: Deleted branches and stashes: commit noted and .patch copy saved.
site.safe5_html: It updates itself when a new version comes out.
site.shot_sub: Animations everywhere and 16-bit music that changes rhythm while she digs.

site.step2_text: Press “Let's dig! ☆” and watch Suri dig, investigate and sniff.
site.step3_text: Check the list (as a tree too) and send to the Trash only what you want.
site.tagline_html: The kawaii meerkat that <mark>digs through your disk</mark> and finds wasted GB: caches, duplicates, forgotten git repos, Claude and Codex data… <mark>You decide, she sweeps!</mark> 🧹✨
site.title: SuriClean · the sweeper meerkat ☆
site.version_note: Latest version from GitHub · open source · no subscription, no ads
site.version_note_v: Version {0} · open source · no subscription, no ads
web.admin.detail: First the password, then a few minutes of digging…
web.admin.done: Yatta~! Now I can see the whole disk, even the locked rooms 🔑✨
web.admin.title: Suri-admin measures the whole disk! 🔐
web.cat.aiTools.explain: Claude Code and Codex histories, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code caches, downloaded models (Hugging Face, Ollama, LM Studio). Recent sessions and models are not preselected.
web.cat.aiTools.sub: Crumbs left by your robot friends 🤖
web.cat.aiTools.title: Claude, Codex & AI
web.cat.bigFiles.explain: Files of 100 MB and up. Nothing is preselected: you decide.
web.cat.bigFiles.scan: Hunting giant monsters! ドドーン
web.cat.bigFiles.sub: The chubbiest monsters in the burrow!
web.cat.bigFiles.title: Giant files
web.cat.buildDeps.explain: Folders that regenerate with a command (npm install, pip install, cargo build, dotnet build…). I preselect those of projects idle for more than 60 days.
web.cat.buildDeps.title: Rebuildable dependencies
web.cat.caches.explain: Caches are only there to speed things up: if you remove them, apps rebuild them when needed. Best to close apps (especially browsers) before cleaning.
web.cat.caches.sub: Magic crumbs that grow back by themselves ✧
web.cat.caches.title: App cache
web.cat.devCaches.explain: Packages downloaded by dependency managers. Everything is re-downloaded on the next build.
web.cat.devCaches.sub: npm, pip, Gradle, Cargo, NuGet, Go…
web.cat.devCaches.title: Developer caches
web.cat.diskMap.explain: Everything taking up space in your user folder, folder by folder (300 MB and up). Nothing gets deleted here: look around and open folders to discover the big beasts.
web.cat.diskMap.scan: Measuring the whole burrow, inch by inch! 📏
web.cat.diskMap.sub: Where did all the GB go? Let's find out ☆
web.cat.diskMap.title: Disk map
web.cat.duplicates.explain: Files of 1 MB and up compared by SHA-256 fingerprint. In each group I keep the “original” copy (💎) and preselect the others. At least one copy always stays.
web.cat.duplicates.title: Twin files
web.cat.gitRepos.explain: For each repo I check the remote, uncommitted changes, important ignored files, unpushed commits and stashes. I only preselect those safe on the remote and idle for 6+ months. The git clone command is saved in Documents.
web.cat.gitRepos.sub: Idle projects you can clone again
web.cat.gitRepos.title: Forgotten Git repos
web.cat.installers.explain: Setup programs and disk images. I preselect those in Downloads and on the Desktop.
web.cat.installers.title: Installers & images
web.cat.logsTemp.explain: Temporary files older than 3 days, crash dumps and error reports. Nobody will miss them.
web.cat.logsTemp.title: Logs & temporary files
web.cat.oldDownloads.explain: Everything that has been in Downloads for more than 90 days. Nothing is preselected.
web.cat.oldDownloads.sub: Stuff in Downloads for more than 3 months
web.cat.oldDownloads.title: Forgotten downloads
web.cat.systemAreas.explain: Outside your folder: system logs and error reports, system temporary files, already-installed updates, memory dumps, downloaded packages, old versions and rotated backups. The administrator password is needed, just once, and they are deleted permanently (they don't go through the Trash). Entries with 🔒 can only be measured as administrator.
web.cat.systemAreas.scan: Suri is exploring the system's rooms! 🏯
web.cat.systemAreas.sub: System logs, temp, updates and dumps 🔐
web.cat.systemAreas.title: System areas

web.cele.recovered: You got back {0} of real space! Sugoi~ ♡

web.copied: Copied! The git clone is safe ♡

web.empty.title: Final clean-up, sparkle-sparkle! 🗑️✨

web.rs.sys.backups_detail: /var/backups · rotated copies of dpkg, apt and passwords
web.rs.sys.dopt_detail: Pieces of updates shared with other PCs: they get re-downloaded
web.rs.sys.hiberfil_detail: Turns off hibernation and fast startup: the PC boots a tiny bit slower
web.rs.sys.rotated_logs_detail: /var/log · old logs already rotated or compressed
web.rs.sys.snap_detail: Previous version kept by snap for rolling back
web.rs.sys.win_temp_detail: C:\Windows\Temp · throwaway files from installations and services
web.rs.sys.windows_old_detail: Only needed to go back to the previous version of Windows · Disk Cleanup removes it
web.rs.sys.winsxs_detail: Removes old versions of components replaced by updates · may take a few minutes
web.rs.sys.wu_detail: Windows Update re-downloads it if it's ever needed
web.scope.text: “Whole disk” asks for the administrator password once and also measures other users' folders and protected system areas.
web.scope.title: Where shall we dig? ☆
web.sort.name: Name
